report.notes: Root cause fixed: both layers now find secret stems anywhere inside a word (_STEMS on _tokens(), which splits at separators and camelCase but not digits), replacing reliance on word boundaries and a fixed prefix list, and treat a 3-8 digit value as a code when a name/label/placeholder/aria label ends in code|pin (punctuation removed), with postal/zip/pincode/country/area/promo/coupon/voucher/referral/barcode/sortcode/ifsc/swift excluded ('gift' left off on purpose). snapshot.js patterns are string-identical; parity test covers STEMS, CODE_END, CODE_EXCLUDE, SENSITIVE_WORDS, RUN_TOGETHER and SHORT_CODE. Tests use 1,442 generated names plus readable controls, checked in Python, PE.normalise and real Chromium (pages of up to 190 fields because of MAX_FIELDS=200); on 627f6b9 the new file gives 774 failures (including all 32 reported-name cases), and after the change all 1625 tests in tests/assist pass. tricky_fields.html gains 14 name-only reported names (s1-s14). A0_QUALIFICATION.md AC7 row corrected, with the earlier claim kept as a recorded correction. Known: Python's second layer reports smspin/cardcode as not sensitive because the page has already emptied the value (no value leaks); the extended exclusions also make 4-8 digit 'Country code'/'Promo code' values readable, which were hidden before. /tmp/uri_review_R3/e2e_leak.py was not available to re-run; the diagnosis's probe.py/e2e.py show 0 leaks. graphify not installed, so the graph update was not run.
